subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should the bundled browser tool make compact goal-shaped reads and post-action change reports the default model-facing behavior, or keep full snapshot reads as the default with efficient mode as an explicit opt-in/configured default?
rationale: Current main has several mitigations, but the requested behavior changes the browser tool contract seen by models and overlaps with plugin/context-engine compression seams and related browser automation issues.

options.title: Default compact browser reads
options.body: Make the browser tool default to compact relevant page state and small action-change reports, while exposing explicit raw/full snapshot actions for escape hatches.

options.title: Keep opt-in efficient mode
options.body: Leave full AI snapshot behavior as the default and document browser.snapshotDefaults.mode plus skill guidance as the supported mitigation.

options.title: Split into narrower browser signals
options.body: Track action diffs, readiness/CAPTCHA/stale-ref signals, and default snapshot shape as separate product decisions under the broader browser field-report cluster.

recommendation.title: Default compact browser reads
recommendation.body: Make the browser tool default to compact relevant page state and small action-change reports, while exposing explicit raw/full snapshot actions for escape hatches.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about bundled browser plugin product scope and current history points to Peter Steinberger on the ownership move and browser docs/snapshot boundary.
